mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a deflationary shock.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a concurrent supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending power and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered periods, or the mechanism fails during a period of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate sales and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous surge in commodity prices.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and price pressures, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: dual inflation and rate hike cycle
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a supply chain shock that boosts inflation independently of monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 6-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which expands corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of aggressive monetary tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the labor force participation rate (implied by a falling unemployment rate while PAYEMS grows) over three consecutive months signals improved labor supply, which boosts productivity and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls AND PAYEMS rises for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a wage-price spiral.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month average for six consecutive months signals a robust housing recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous rise in mortgage rates that offsets the housing demand signal.
